punchline: On a game show with real money, contestants took bigger risks both after losing hopes and after beating them.
thirty_sec: Thaler and Eric Johnson found that people who are ahead in a gamble take more risks with their winnings. Years later, Post, van den Assem, Baltussen and Thaler tested the idea on the game show Deal or No Deal, where large sums were at stake. Earlier outcomes largely explained contestants' choices: risk aversion fell after both shattered and surpassed expectations. The past was steering choices that theory says should look forward only.
